# 07 — Security Model

## 1. Identity

* One real officer = one `Officer` row. No per-portal user tables.
* `officer_id` is an identifier only; it encodes **no** authorization.
* Officer IDs are generated by Central IT via `OfficerIDService`
  (format configurable via `OFFICER_ID_PREFIX` / `OFFICER_ID_WIDTH`).

## 2. Authentication

* Django auth + custom backend; passwords hashed with Django PBKDF2.
* Second factor abstracted behind `AuthenticationFactor` + `SecurityCodeService`
  (salted HMAC digest; ready to swap in TOTP).
* First-run secret code: provisioned by IT, hashed at rest, must be changed on
  activation; enrolment screen re-verifies password first.

## 3. Authorization

* Central `AuthorizationService`; deny by default; complete mediation;
  RBAC + clearance + scope + (future) case/resource/action.

## 4. Session

* Rotation on login; server-side expiry + inactivity; secure/HttpOnly/SameSite
  cookies; CSRF everywhere; logout flushes session; re-auth gate for sensitive
  operations.

## 5. Web security headers

* `SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT`, `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE`, `CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE`,
  `SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY`, `CSRF_COOKIE_HTTPONLY`,
  `SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS`, `X_FRAME_OPTIONS=DENY`,
  `SECURE_CONTENT_TYPE_NOSNIFF`, `SECURE_REFERRER_POLICY=same-origin`,
  `SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER` for TLS-terminating proxies.

## 6. Secrets management

* `SECRET_KEY`, DB password, and all MFA/OTP secrets come from environment
  variables. `.env.example` committed; real `.env` git-ignored.

## 7. Audit & accountability

* Every security-sensitive event recorded with WHO / WHAT / WHEN / CONTEXT /
  RESULT.
* Denials are logged as aggressively as grants; repeated denials raise
  `SecurityEvent` alerts.
* Audit records are append-only (no update/delete views in this MVP).

## 8. Separation of duties

* `IT_ADMIN` (identity administration) vs `SECURITY_ADMIN` (security ops +
  audit) vs investigation data access vs system configuration.
* `is_superuser` exists only for development/emergency; production flows never
  depend on it.

## 9. Impersonation

* No "login as officer" for any role. Reserved future break-glass would require
  reason + duration + authorization + full audit and would preserve the
  original identity. Not implemented now.

## 10. Failure handling

* Generic, non-revealing error messages; detailed reasons only for authorized
  security/audit viewers via `SecurityEvent.details`.
